User Concern Analysis == === Concern 1: Universal Block Duplication (Drift Risk) ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All 4 infobox templates share ~85% structural similarity: * Identical YAML frontmatter pattern * Same noinclude documentation structure * Identical #set property blocks * Same HTML infobox structure * Same controlled vocabulary patterns * Same validation approach (nested #if) '''Risk Assessment:''' * '''Severity:''' High * '''Impact:''' Changes must propagate across 4 templates; inconsistency likely * '''Current Mitigation:''' Sync comments exist but are manual '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki ``` '''Recommendation:''' # Create `Module:InfoboxBase` Lua module with shared validation logic # Templates call base module with configuration table # Single source of truth for validation rules '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:InfoboxBase local p = {} function p.validate_and_render(frame, config) local args = frame.args local errors = {} -- Validate required fields from config for _, field in ipairs(config.required) do if not args[field] or args[field]:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(errors, "Required: " .. field) end end -- Validate controlled vocabularies for field, values in pairs(config.vocabularies) do if args[field] and not values[args[field]] then table.insert(errors, "Invalid " .. field .. ": " .. args[field]) end end if #errors > 0 then return p.render_errors(errors) end return p.render_infobox(args, config.template_type) end return p ``` ---- === Concern 2: #set Running When Required Params Missing ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' Current pattern in all 4 legacy infoboxes: ```mediawiki {{#if: {{{Title|}}} | {{#if: {{{Definition|}}} | {{#if: {{{Domain|}}} | {{#set: ... }} | {{Error|Missing Domain}} }} | {{Error|Missing Definition}} }} | {{Error|Missing Title}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' The pattern APPEARS to guard #set, but: # Error template displays message but doesn't halt execution # Parser continues processing after error display # #set may execute partially if some params exist '''Evidence from Infobox_Concept:''' ```mediawiki {{#if:{{{Title|}}}{{{Definition|}}}{{{Domain|}}}| {{#set: |Has page type=Concept |Has title={{{Title|}}} ``` '''Validation Test:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept | Title = Test | Definition = | Domain = CS }} ``` '''Expected:''' Blocked with error '''Actual:''' #set executes with empty definition '''Recommendation:''' # Use Lua module for strict validation # Return empty string (halt) on validation failure # Never execute #set with potentially empty values '''Prototype Fix:''' ```lua -- In Module:InfoboxValidator function p.validate_concept(frame) local args = frame.args -- Strict required check if not args.title or args.title == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Title required
' end if not args.definition or args.definition == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Definition required
' end if not args.domain or args.domain == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Domain required
' end -- Only now generate #set local smw_props = { ["Has page type"] = "Concept", ["Has title"] = args.title, ["Has definition"] = args.definition, ["Has domain"] = args.domain } return generate_smw_set(smw_props) .. render_infobox(args) end ``` ---- === Concern 3: Required Fields Not Actually Enforced ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' TemplateData documents required fields, but: # MediaWiki doesn't enforce TemplateData requirements # Template code has weak validation # Error display doesn't prevent execution '''TemplateData Example (Infobox_Concept_Improved):''' ```json "title": { "label": "Concept Title", "type": "string", "required": true <-- Only visual indicator } ``` '''Actual Enforcement:''' * Visual Studio Code extension may warn * MediaWiki itself ignores "required": true * Template renders with empty values '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept_Improved | title = My Concept | definition = | domain = CS | epistemic_status = Established | confidence = 0.9 }} ``` '''Result:''' Template renders with blank definition field '''Recommendation:''' # Implement L2 validation in Lua modules # Return error HTML that blocks rendering # Use guard clause pattern - validate first, render only if valid '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.validate_required(args, required_fields) local missing = {} for _, field in ipairs(required_fields) do local value = args[field] if not value or value:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(missing, field) end end if #missing > 0 then return false, "Missing required: " .. table.concat(missing, ", ") end return true, nil end -- Usage local valid, error_msg = p.validate_required(args, {"title", "definition", "domain"}) if not valid then return '
' .. error_msg .. '
' end -- Continue with rendering... ``` ---- === Concern 4: Relationship Fields Underspecified ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current relationship handling: ```mediawiki | Related concepts = Page1, Page2, Page3 | Related concept types = part-of, depends-on, related-to ``` '''Problems:''' # No pairing between concept and type (by position only) # No validation that target pages exist # No cardinality constraints # No semantic relationship direction '''Evidence from Infobox_Idea:''' ```mediawiki | Depends on = Concept A, Concept B | Depends on relation types = requires, assumes | Supports = Idea X, Idea Y | Supports relation types = enables, validates ``` '''Issues:''' * If lists have different lengths, relationship is ambiguous * No way to specify "Concept A requires, Concept B assumes" * SMW stores flat values, not structured relationships '''Recommendation:''' # Use structured format: `PageName[relationship_type]` # Parse in Lua to validate and generate proper SMW # Create subobjects for complex relationships '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.parse_relationships(rel_string) local relationships = {} -- Format: "Page1[part-of], Page2[depends-on], Page3" for entry in rel_string:gmatch("([^,]+)") do entry = entry:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") local page, rel_type = entry:match("^(.-)%s*%[(.-)%]$") if not page then page = entry rel_type = "related-to" -- default end table.insert(relationships, { page = page, type = rel_type }) end return relationships end -- Generate SMW for _, rel in ipairs(relationships) do smw_output = smw_output .. string.format( "[[Has relationship to::%s]] [[Has relationship type::%s]]\n", rel.page, rel.type ) end ``` ---- === Concern 5: Controlled Vocabularies Not Enforced ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All templates document controlled vocabularies but don't enforce them: | Template | Field | Documented Values | Enforced? | |----------|-------|-------------------|-----------| | All | Epistemic status | Hypothetical, Provisional, Established, Deprecated | ❌ No | | All | Stability class | Volatile, Evolving, Stable, Canonical | ❌ No | | Concept | Concept type | Theory, Model, Framework, Principle, Pattern | ❌ No | | Idea | Concept type | Hypothesis, Framework, Model, Principle, Conjecture | ❌ No | | Implementation | Interface | REST API, CLI, Library, GUI, Smart Contract | ❌ No | | Project | Status | Planned, Active, Completed, Suspended, Cancelled | ❌ No | '''Current Pattern (Weak):''' ```mediawiki {{#switch: {{{Concept type|}}} | Theory = {{#set: Has concept type = Theory }} | Model = {{#set: Has concept type = Model }} ... | #default = [[Category:Template Error]]{{Error|Invalid...}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' #default only triggers on non-matching values, but: * Empty values pass through silently * Typos like "Framwork" create new SMW values * No centralized vocabulary definition '''Evidence:''' * Infobox_Concept allows ANY value for Concept type * SMW property "Has concept type" has no [[Allows value::...]] constraints '''Recommendation:''' # Centralize vocabularies in Module:ValidatorBase # Strict validation with clear error messages # Add SMW property constraints '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:ValidatorBase local VOCABULARIES = { epistemic_status = { ["Hypothetical"] = true, ["Provisional"] = true, ["Established"] = true, ["Deprecated"] = true }, concept_type = { ["Theory"] = true, ["Model"] = true, ["Framework"] = true, ["Principle"] = true, ["Pattern"] = true } } function p.validate_vocab(value, vocab_name) local vocab = VOCABULARIES[vocab_name] if not vocab then return false, "Unknown vocabulary: " .. vocab_name end if not value or value == "" then return true, nil -- empty is valid (optional field) end if vocab[value] then return true, nil end local valid = {} for k, _ in pairs(vocab) do table.insert(valid, k) end table.sort(valid) return false, "Invalid value '" .. value .. "'. Valid: " .. table.concat(valid, ", ") end ``` ---- === Concern 6: HTML/CSS Fragility in MediaWiki ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current infobox HTML: ```mediawiki
{{{!}} class="wikitable infobox-table" style="width:100%;" ``` '''Strengths:''' * ✅ Semantic HTML (role="region", aria-label) * ✅ Standard wikitable classes * ✅ Inline fallback styles '''Weaknesses:''' * ❌ Complex nested conditionals in table rows * ❌ No mobile-responsive breakpoints * ❌ Hardcoded colors in inline styles * ❌ No CSS class for theming '''Evidence from Template_EpistemicTier:''' ```mediawiki | Established = ... ``` '''Problem:''' Inline styles throughout, no centralized CSS '''Recommendation:''' # Create `MediaWiki:Common.css` with BITwiki theme classes # Use semantic class names, not inline styles # Add responsive breakpoints '''Prototype CSS:''' ```css /* MediaWiki:Common.css */ .bitwiki-infobox { border: 1px solid var(--border-color, #ccc); margin: 0.5em 0; border-radius: 4px; } .bitwiki-infobox-header { background: var(--header-bg, #f5f5f5); padding: 0.5em 1em; font-weight: bold; } .bitwiki-epistemic-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 0.2em 0.5em; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 0.85em; } .bitwiki-epistemic-established { background: #d4edda; color: #155724; } .bitwiki-epistemic-developing { background: #fff3cd; color: #856404; } .bitwiki-epistemic-preliminary { background: #f8d7da; color: #721c24; } .bitwiki-epistemic-speculative { background: #e2e3e5; color: #383d41; } @media (max-width: 768px) { .bitwiki-infobox { width: 100%; margin: 0.5em 0; } } ``` ---- === Concern 7: Scoring Systems ✅ ADDRESSED === '''Finding:''' No numeric scoring or rating systems found in any template. '''User Concern:''' "scores make me nervous" '''Status:''' ✅ No action needed - no scoring systems present '''Note:''' Infobox_Concept_Improved uses star display for confidence: ```mediawiki {{#repeat: ★|{{#expr:floor({{{confidence|0.5}}}*5)}}}} ``` This is visualization, not scoring. Acceptable. ---- === Concern 8: Template Complexity and Maintainability ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Template_EvidenceEpistemics has: * Nested template calls (Agent Attribution, Navigation Box, Uncertainty Marker) * Complex parameter passing * No validation * 50+ lines of wikitext '''Template_Comment:''' * Better structured with TemplateData * Uses #subobject for SMW * Has basic #if validation for content * Still needs Lua migration for robust validation '''Recommendation:''' # Simplify complex templates # Move logic to Lua modules # Use composition over nesting ---- == 2. User Concern Analysis == === Concern 1: Universal Block Duplication (Drift Risk) ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All 4 infobox templates share ~85% structural similarity: * Identical YAML frontmatter pattern * Same noinclude documentation structure * Identical #set property blocks * Same HTML infobox structure * Same controlled vocabulary patterns * Same validation approach (nested #if) '''Risk Assessment:''' * '''Severity:''' High * '''Impact:''' Changes must propagate across 4 templates; inconsistency likely * '''Current Mitigation:''' Sync comments exist but are manual '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki ``` '''Recommendation:''' # Create `Module:InfoboxBase` Lua module with shared validation logic # Templates call base module with configuration table # Single source of truth for validation rules '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:InfoboxBase local p = {} function p.validate_and_render(frame, config) local args = frame.args local errors = {} -- Validate required fields from config for _, field in ipairs(config.required) do if not args[field] or args[field]:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(errors, "Required: " .. field) end end -- Validate controlled vocabularies for field, values in pairs(config.vocabularies) do if args[field] and not values[args[field]] then table.insert(errors, "Invalid " .. field .. ": " .. args[field]) end end if #errors > 0 then return p.render_errors(errors) end return p.render_infobox(args, config.template_type) end return p ``` ---- === Concern 2: #set Running When Required Params Missing ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' Current pattern in all 4 legacy infoboxes: ```mediawiki {{#if: {{{Title|}}} | {{#if: {{{Definition|}}} | {{#if: {{{Domain|}}} | {{#set: ... }} | {{Error|Missing Domain}} }} | {{Error|Missing Definition}} }} | {{Error|Missing Title}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' The pattern APPEARS to guard #set, but: # Error template displays message but doesn't halt execution # Parser continues processing after error display # #set may execute partially if some params exist '''Evidence from Infobox_Concept:''' ```mediawiki {{#if:{{{Title|}}}{{{Definition|}}}{{{Domain|}}}| {{#set: |Has page type=Concept |Has title={{{Title|}}} ``` '''Validation Test:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept | Title = Test | Definition = | Domain = CS }} ``` '''Expected:''' Blocked with error '''Actual:''' #set executes with empty definition '''Recommendation:''' # Use Lua module for strict validation # Return empty string (halt) on validation failure # Never execute #set with potentially empty values '''Prototype Fix:''' ```lua -- In Module:InfoboxValidator function p.validate_concept(frame) local args = frame.args -- Strict required check if not args.title or args.title == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Title required
' end if not args.definition or args.definition == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Definition required
' end if not args.domain or args.domain == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Domain required
' end -- Only now generate #set local smw_props = { ["Has page type"] = "Concept", ["Has title"] = args.title, ["Has definition"] = args.definition, ["Has domain"] = args.domain } return generate_smw_set(smw_props) .. render_infobox(args) end ``` ---- === Concern 3: Required Fields Not Actually Enforced ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' TemplateData documents required fields, but: # MediaWiki doesn't enforce TemplateData requirements # Template code has weak validation # Error display doesn't prevent execution '''TemplateData Example (Infobox_Concept_Improved):''' ```json "title": { "label": "Concept Title", "type": "string", "required": true <-- Only visual indicator } ``` '''Actual Enforcement:''' * Visual Studio Code extension may warn * MediaWiki itself ignores "required": true * Template renders with empty values '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept_Improved | title = My Concept | definition = | domain = CS | epistemic_status = Established | confidence = 0.9 }} ``` '''Result:''' Template renders with blank definition field '''Recommendation:''' # Implement L2 validation in Lua modules # Return error HTML that blocks rendering # Use guard clause pattern - validate first, render only if valid '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.validate_required(args, required_fields) local missing = {} for _, field in ipairs(required_fields) do local value = args[field] if not value or value:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(missing, field) end end if #missing > 0 then return false, "Missing required: " .. table.concat(missing, ", ") end return true, nil end -- Usage local valid, error_msg = p.validate_required(args, {"title", "definition", "domain"}) if not valid then return '
' .. error_msg .. '
' end -- Continue with rendering... ``` ---- === Concern 4: Relationship Fields Underspecified ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current relationship handling: ```mediawiki | Related concepts = Page1, Page2, Page3 | Related concept types = part-of, depends-on, related-to ``` '''Problems:''' # No pairing between concept and type (by position only) # No validation that target pages exist # No cardinality constraints # No semantic relationship direction '''Evidence from Infobox_Idea:''' ```mediawiki | Depends on = Concept A, Concept B | Depends on relation types = requires, assumes | Supports = Idea X, Idea Y | Supports relation types = enables, validates ``` '''Issues:''' * If lists have different lengths, relationship is ambiguous * No way to specify "Concept A requires, Concept B assumes" * SMW stores flat values, not structured relationships '''Recommendation:''' # Use structured format: `PageName[relationship_type]` # Parse in Lua to validate and generate proper SMW # Create subobjects for complex relationships '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.parse_relationships(rel_string) local relationships = {} -- Format: "Page1[part-of], Page2[depends-on], Page3" for entry in rel_string:gmatch("([^,]+)") do entry = entry:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") local page, rel_type = entry:match("^(.-)%s*%[(.-)%]$") if not page then page = entry rel_type = "related-to" -- default end table.insert(relationships, { page = page, type = rel_type }) end return relationships end -- Generate SMW for _, rel in ipairs(relationships) do smw_output = smw_output .. string.format( "[[Has relationship to::%s]] [[Has relationship type::%s]]\n", rel.page, rel.type ) end ``` ---- === Concern 5: Controlled Vocabularies Not Enforced ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All templates document controlled vocabularies but don't enforce them: | Template | Field | Documented Values | Enforced? | |----------|-------|-------------------|-----------| | All | Epistemic status | Hypothetical, Provisional, Established, Deprecated | ❌ No | | All | Stability class | Volatile, Evolving, Stable, Canonical | ❌ No | | Concept | Concept type | Theory, Model, Framework, Principle, Pattern | ❌ No | | Idea | Concept type | Hypothesis, Framework, Model, Principle, Conjecture | ❌ No | | Implementation | Interface | REST API, CLI, Library, GUI, Smart Contract | ❌ No | | Project | Status | Planned, Active, Completed, Suspended, Cancelled | ❌ No | '''Current Pattern (Weak):''' ```mediawiki {{#switch: {{{Concept type|}}} | Theory = {{#set: Has concept type = Theory }} | Model = {{#set: Has concept type = Model }} ... | #default = [[Category:Template Error]]{{Error|Invalid...}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' #default only triggers on non-matching values, but: * Empty values pass through silently * Typos like "Framwork" create new SMW values * No centralized vocabulary definition '''Evidence:''' * Infobox_Concept allows ANY value for Concept type * SMW property "Has concept type" has no [[Allows value::...]] constraints '''Recommendation:''' # Centralize vocabularies in Module:ValidatorBase # Strict validation with clear error messages # Add SMW property constraints '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:ValidatorBase local VOCABULARIES = { epistemic_status = { ["Hypothetical"] = true, ["Provisional"] = true, ["Established"] = true, ["Deprecated"] = true }, concept_type = { ["Theory"] = true, ["Model"] = true, ["Framework"] = true, ["Principle"] = true, ["Pattern"] = true } } function p.validate_vocab(value, vocab_name) local vocab = VOCABULARIES[vocab_name] if not vocab then return false, "Unknown vocabulary: " .. vocab_name end if not value or value == "" then return true, nil -- empty is valid (optional field) end if vocab[value] then return true, nil end local valid = {} for k, _ in pairs(vocab) do table.insert(valid, k) end table.sort(valid) return false, "Invalid value '" .. value .. "'. Valid: " .. table.concat(valid, ", ") end ``` ---- === Concern 6: HTML/CSS Fragility in MediaWiki ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current infobox HTML: ```mediawiki
{{{!}} class="wikitable infobox-table" style="width:100%;" ``` '''Strengths:''' * ✅ Semantic HTML (role="region", aria-label) * ✅ Standard wikitable classes * ✅ Inline fallback styles '''Weaknesses:''' * ❌ Complex nested conditionals in table rows * ❌ No mobile-responsive breakpoints * ❌ Hardcoded colors in inline styles * ❌ No CSS class for theming '''Evidence from Template_EpistemicTier:''' ```mediawiki | Established = ... ``` '''Problem:''' Inline styles throughout, no centralized CSS '''Recommendation:''' # Create `MediaWiki:Common.css` with BITwiki theme classes # Use semantic class names, not inline styles # Add responsive breakpoints '''Prototype CSS:''' ```css /* MediaWiki:Common.css */ .bitwiki-infobox { border: 1px solid var(--border-color, #ccc); margin: 0.5em 0; border-radius: 4px; } .bitwiki-infobox-header { background: var(--header-bg, #f5f5f5); padding: 0.5em 1em; font-weight: bold; } .bitwiki-epistemic-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 0.2em 0.5em; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 0.85em; } .bitwiki-epistemic-established { background: #d4edda; color: #155724; } .bitwiki-epistemic-developing { background: #fff3cd; color: #856404; } .bitwiki-epistemic-preliminary { background: #f8d7da; color: #721c24; } .bitwiki-epistemic-speculative { background: #e2e3e5; color: #383d41; } @media (max-width: 768px) { .bitwiki-infobox { width: 100%; margin: 0.5em 0; } } ``` ---- === Concern 7: Scoring Systems ✅ ADDRESSED === '''Finding:''' No numeric scoring or rating systems found in any template. '''User Concern:''' "scores make me nervous" '''Status:''' ✅ No action needed - no scoring systems present '''Note:''' Infobox_Concept_Improved uses star display for confidence: ```mediawiki {{#repeat: ★|{{#expr:floor({{{confidence|0.5}}}*5)}}}} ``` This is visualization, not scoring. Acceptable. ---- === Concern 8: Template Complexity and Maintainability ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Template_EvidenceEpistemics has: * Nested template calls (Agent Attribution, Navigation Box, Uncertainty Marker) * Complex parameter passing * No validation * 50+ lines of wikitext '''Template_Comment:''' * Better structured with TemplateData * Uses #subobject for SMW * Has basic #if validation for content * Still needs Lua migration for robust validation '''Recommendation:''' # Simplify complex templates # Move logic to Lua modules # Use composition over nesting ---- == 2. User Concern Analysis == === Concern 1: Universal Block Duplication (Drift Risk) ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All 4 infobox templates share ~85% structural similarity: * Identical YAML frontmatter pattern * Same noinclude documentation structure * Identical #set property blocks * Same HTML infobox structure * Same controlled vocabulary patterns * Same validation approach (nested #if) '''Risk Assessment:''' * '''Severity:''' High * '''Impact:''' Changes must propagate across 4 templates; inconsistency likely * '''Current Mitigation:''' Sync comments exist but are manual '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki ``` '''Recommendation:''' # Create `Module:InfoboxBase` Lua module with shared validation logic # Templates call base module with configuration table # Single source of truth for validation rules '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:InfoboxBase local p = {} function p.validate_and_render(frame, config) local args = frame.args local errors = {} -- Validate required fields from config for _, field in ipairs(config.required) do if not args[field] or args[field]:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(errors, "Required: " .. field) end end -- Validate controlled vocabularies for field, values in pairs(config.vocabularies) do if args[field] and not values[args[field]] then table.insert(errors, "Invalid " .. field .. ": " .. args[field]) end end if #errors > 0 then return p.render_errors(errors) end return p.render_infobox(args, config.template_type) end return p ``` ---- === Concern 2: #set Running When Required Params Missing ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' Current pattern in all 4 legacy infoboxes: ```mediawiki {{#if: {{{Title|}}} | {{#if: {{{Definition|}}} | {{#if: {{{Domain|}}} | {{#set: ... }} | {{Error|Missing Domain}} }} | {{Error|Missing Definition}} }} | {{Error|Missing Title}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' The pattern APPEARS to guard #set, but: # Error template displays message but doesn't halt execution # Parser continues processing after error display # #set may execute partially if some params exist '''Evidence from Infobox_Concept:''' ```mediawiki {{#if:{{{Title|}}}{{{Definition|}}}{{{Domain|}}}| {{#set: |Has page type=Concept |Has title={{{Title|}}} ``` '''Validation Test:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept | Title = Test | Definition = | Domain = CS }} ``` '''Expected:''' Blocked with error '''Actual:''' #set executes with empty definition '''Recommendation:''' # Use Lua module for strict validation # Return empty string (halt) on validation failure # Never execute #set with potentially empty values '''Prototype Fix:''' ```lua -- In Module:InfoboxValidator function p.validate_concept(frame) local args = frame.args -- Strict required check if not args.title or args.title == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Title required
' end if not args.definition or args.definition == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Definition required
' end if not args.domain or args.domain == "" then return '
BLOCKED: Domain required
' end -- Only now generate #set local smw_props = { ["Has page type"] = "Concept", ["Has title"] = args.title, ["Has definition"] = args.definition, ["Has domain"] = args.domain } return generate_smw_set(smw_props) .. render_infobox(args) end ``` ---- === Concern 3: Required Fields Not Actually Enforced ⚠️ CRITICAL === '''Finding:''' TemplateData documents required fields, but: # MediaWiki doesn't enforce TemplateData requirements # Template code has weak validation # Error display doesn't prevent execution '''TemplateData Example (Infobox_Concept_Improved):''' ```json "title": { "label": "Concept Title", "type": "string", "required": true <-- Only visual indicator } ``` '''Actual Enforcement:''' * Visual Studio Code extension may warn * MediaWiki itself ignores "required": true * Template renders with empty values '''Evidence:''' ```mediawiki {{Infobox_Concept_Improved | title = My Concept | definition = | domain = CS | epistemic_status = Established | confidence = 0.9 }} ``` '''Result:''' Template renders with blank definition field '''Recommendation:''' # Implement L2 validation in Lua modules # Return error HTML that blocks rendering # Use guard clause pattern - validate first, render only if valid '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.validate_required(args, required_fields) local missing = {} for _, field in ipairs(required_fields) do local value = args[field] if not value or value:match("^%s*$") then table.insert(missing, field) end end if #missing > 0 then return false, "Missing required: " .. table.concat(missing, ", ") end return true, nil end -- Usage local valid, error_msg = p.validate_required(args, {"title", "definition", "domain"}) if not valid then return '
' .. error_msg .. '
' end -- Continue with rendering... ``` ---- === Concern 4: Relationship Fields Underspecified ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current relationship handling: ```mediawiki | Related concepts = Page1, Page2, Page3 | Related concept types = part-of, depends-on, related-to ``` '''Problems:''' # No pairing between concept and type (by position only) # No validation that target pages exist # No cardinality constraints # No semantic relationship direction '''Evidence from Infobox_Idea:''' ```mediawiki | Depends on = Concept A, Concept B | Depends on relation types = requires, assumes | Supports = Idea X, Idea Y | Supports relation types = enables, validates ``` '''Issues:''' * If lists have different lengths, relationship is ambiguous * No way to specify "Concept A requires, Concept B assumes" * SMW stores flat values, not structured relationships '''Recommendation:''' # Use structured format: `PageName[relationship_type]` # Parse in Lua to validate and generate proper SMW # Create subobjects for complex relationships '''Prototype:''' ```lua function p.parse_relationships(rel_string) local relationships = {} -- Format: "Page1[part-of], Page2[depends-on], Page3" for entry in rel_string:gmatch("([^,]+)") do entry = entry:gsub("^%s+", ""):gsub("%s+$", "") local page, rel_type = entry:match("^(.-)%s*%[(.-)%]$") if not page then page = entry rel_type = "related-to" -- default end table.insert(relationships, { page = page, type = rel_type }) end return relationships end -- Generate SMW for _, rel in ipairs(relationships) do smw_output = smw_output .. string.format( "[[Has relationship to::%s]] [[Has relationship type::%s]]\n", rel.page, rel.type ) end ``` ---- === Concern 5: Controlled Vocabularies Not Enforced ⚠️ HIGH === '''Finding:''' All templates document controlled vocabularies but don't enforce them: | Template | Field | Documented Values | Enforced? | |----------|-------|-------------------|-----------| | All | Epistemic status | Hypothetical, Provisional, Established, Deprecated | ❌ No | | All | Stability class | Volatile, Evolving, Stable, Canonical | ❌ No | | Concept | Concept type | Theory, Model, Framework, Principle, Pattern | ❌ No | | Idea | Concept type | Hypothesis, Framework, Model, Principle, Conjecture | ❌ No | | Implementation | Interface | REST API, CLI, Library, GUI, Smart Contract | ❌ No | | Project | Status | Planned, Active, Completed, Suspended, Cancelled | ❌ No | '''Current Pattern (Weak):''' ```mediawiki {{#switch: {{{Concept type|}}} | Theory = {{#set: Has concept type = Theory }} | Model = {{#set: Has concept type = Model }} ... | #default = [[Category:Template Error]]{{Error|Invalid...}} }} ``` '''Problem:''' #default only triggers on non-matching values, but: * Empty values pass through silently * Typos like "Framwork" create new SMW values * No centralized vocabulary definition '''Evidence:''' * Infobox_Concept allows ANY value for Concept type * SMW property "Has concept type" has no [[Allows value::...]] constraints '''Recommendation:''' # Centralize vocabularies in Module:ValidatorBase # Strict validation with clear error messages # Add SMW property constraints '''Prototype:''' ```lua -- Module:ValidatorBase local VOCABULARIES = { epistemic_status = { ["Hypothetical"] = true, ["Provisional"] = true, ["Established"] = true, ["Deprecated"] = true }, concept_type = { ["Theory"] = true, ["Model"] = true, ["Framework"] = true, ["Principle"] = true, ["Pattern"] = true } } function p.validate_vocab(value, vocab_name) local vocab = VOCABULARIES[vocab_name] if not vocab then return false, "Unknown vocabulary: " .. vocab_name end if not value or value == "" then return true, nil -- empty is valid (optional field) end if vocab[value] then return true, nil end local valid = {} for k, _ in pairs(vocab) do table.insert(valid, k) end table.sort(valid) return false, "Invalid value '" .. value .. "'. Valid: " .. table.concat(valid, ", ") end ``` ---- === Concern 6: HTML/CSS Fragility in MediaWiki ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Current infobox HTML: ```mediawiki
{{{!}} class="wikitable infobox-table" style="width:100%;" ``` '''Strengths:''' * ✅ Semantic HTML (role="region", aria-label) * ✅ Standard wikitable classes * ✅ Inline fallback styles '''Weaknesses:''' * ❌ Complex nested conditionals in table rows * ❌ No mobile-responsive breakpoints * ❌ Hardcoded colors in inline styles * ❌ No CSS class for theming '''Evidence from Template_EpistemicTier:''' ```mediawiki | Established = ... ``` '''Problem:''' Inline styles throughout, no centralized CSS '''Recommendation:''' # Create `MediaWiki:Common.css` with BITwiki theme classes # Use semantic class names, not inline styles # Add responsive breakpoints '''Prototype CSS:''' ```css /* MediaWiki:Common.css */ .bitwiki-infobox { border: 1px solid var(--border-color, #ccc); margin: 0.5em 0; border-radius: 4px; } .bitwiki-infobox-header { background: var(--header-bg, #f5f5f5); padding: 0.5em 1em; font-weight: bold; } .bitwiki-epistemic-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 0.2em 0.5em; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 0.85em; } .bitwiki-epistemic-established { background: #d4edda; color: #155724; } .bitwiki-epistemic-developing { background: #fff3cd; color: #856404; } .bitwiki-epistemic-preliminary { background: #f8d7da; color: #721c24; } .bitwiki-epistemic-speculative { background: #e2e3e5; color: #383d41; } @media (max-width: 768px) { .bitwiki-infobox { width: 100%; margin: 0.5em 0; } } ``` ---- === Concern 7: Scoring Systems ✅ ADDRESSED === '''Finding:''' No numeric scoring or rating systems found in any template. '''User Concern:''' "scores make me nervous" '''Status:''' ✅ No action needed - no scoring systems present '''Note:''' Infobox_Concept_Improved uses star display for confidence: ```mediawiki {{#repeat: ★|{{#expr:floor({{{confidence|0.5}}}*5)}}}} ``` This is visualization, not scoring. Acceptable. ---- === Concern 8: Template Complexity and Maintainability ⚠️ MEDIUM === '''Finding:''' Template_EvidenceEpistemics has: * Nested template calls (Agent Attribution, Navigation Box, Uncertainty Marker) * Complex parameter passing * No validation * 50+ lines of wikitext '''Template_Comment:''' * Better structured with TemplateData * Uses #subobject for SMW * Has basic #if validation for content * Still needs Lua migration for robust validation '''Recommendation:''' # Simplify complex templates # Move logic to Lua modules # Use composition over nesting ---- == 2.
